howtogo.configuration.ui_theme.tooltip:
Which style this mod's interfaces are drawn in.

dark: always the black style the mod has always had.
light: always the white style -- white sheets, near-black text and Google Maps' blue for anything that can be acted on, keeping the same simple, flat, text-and-hairline look.
auto (the default): follows the world -- white while the sky is bright, black once it is dark, and always black in the Nether, the End and any other dimension without a sky. It reads the same sky-brightness value the sky itself is shaded by, so it turns over when the sun does and a thunderstorm darkens it too.

A client setting: nothing in the world changes and nothing is sent to a server. A change takes effect on the next frame, across every screen this mod opens, including the navigation panel and the destination page inside MCphone.
howtogo.configuration.map_display_mode.t:
Where the map half of navigation is drawn.

HUD panel (the default): this mod's own navigation panel draws it -- a card in the corner holding a small rotating map with the roads, the route, the turn markers and the destination, and the trip readout under it. It works with nothing else installed.
Xaero's Minimap: the route, the turn markers and the destination are drawn over Xaero's Minimap instead, and this mod's HUD keeps only a small card carrying what a map cannot show -- the turn arrow, the distance to the turn, what is left of the trip and the progress bar.

The second answer needs Xaero's Minimap (id "xaerominimap") installed and this build compiled against it. If either is missing, the HUD panel is used instead and one line in the log says what was missing.

A client setting: nothing in the world changes and nothing is sent to a server. On NeoForge a change takes effect on the next frame; the Fabric file is read at startup, as every value in it is.
howtogo.configuration.compact_hud_anchor:
Which corner the small readout-only card hangs from, in the Xaero's Minimap display mode.

The default is the bottom-left: Xaero's Minimap puts its own map in the top-left corner by default, so the bottom of the screen keeps this card off it and out of the way of everything at eye level. A player whose chat is long, or who has moved Xaero's Minimap there, can move the card with the offsets below.
howtogo.configuration.compact_hud_offset: How far the small readout card sits from its corner's left or right edge, in pixels at the current GUI scale. Zero is the standard screen margin; positive values move it further into the screen.
How far the small readout card sits from its corner's top or bottom edge, in pixels at the current GUI scale. Zero is the standard screen margin; positive values move it further into the screen.
